description: Navigate back in the app or through system navigation. The in-app mode targets the app navigation stack; system targets platform back behavior. On iOS both modes press the navigation bar system back button (identifier BackButton) only when exactly one hittable one is found in a readable accessibility tree, and succeed only when the number of navigation bars, the number of back buttons, or a back button title then changes (a bar title or a moved back button alone never counts, so a pop that keeps the same back button title and bar count reports back_swipe_unverified); with no such button, two candidates, or an unreadable tree, they swipe from the left edge instead (on an iPad whose app window cannot be resolved, only while the app fills the screen) and succeed only when the app screen changes. Reason back_swipe_no_change: the swipe was sent and the screen did not change; a visible back or close control is an alternative. Reason back_swipe_unverified: the button was pressed but the navigation bar's back buttons did not change within 1 s or on one more read after it, or the swipe may or may not have navigated, because the screen kept changing before it or could not be sampled after it; the resulting screen is unconfirmed. Reason back_swipe_not_dispatched, or a screen that cannot be sampled before the swipe, means nothing was sent. An app with a left-edge drawer may open the drawer instead. A visible back or close control can be targeted directly by its ref. Times out after 90s; a caller-supplied budget extends it.

device.description: Device name; ids go in udid or serial.

serial.description: Android, HarmonyOS, or Vega VVD serial.

settle.description: Once the UI goes quiet, return the diff vs the pre-action tree. Best-effort; never fails the action.

settleQuietMs.description: Settle: quiet window in ms (default 500, 300 on iOS simulator; broad iOS screen swaps hold at least 1500).

name: back
title: Navigate back in the app or system
